slice: S3 native selection and owner lifecycle

source_evidence.fact: HostState/AppState separation, real window origin gate and existing lock-order precedent
WORK registry/leases remain distinct; lexical document_root_key is not native path proof
S2 authority context explicitly delegates real owner/native authentication to S3

rules.name: Actual caller
rules.contract: Use injected WebviewWindow label and URL, never JSON caller fields. Propose reusing existing guard_owner_caller_allowed policy: main only, no explicit port, tauri://localhost or http(s)://tauri.localhost. Existing command allowlist and capability permission are additional gates, not substitutes. Development localhost:1420 remains denied unless separately approved.

rules.name: One owner generation
rules.contract: Propose one active wizard owner per main-window instance, identified by server-issued runtime epoch and monotonically changing owner generation. DispatchHost owns wizard records separately from WORK project registry; WORK continues owning registered projects/leases. Opening wizard does not register a project, change HostSettings or acquire a Run lease.

rules.name: Native selection
rules.contract: Only an authenticated native picker result can mint an opaque selection ID. Record binds canonical parent/root, selection purpose, window instance and owner generation. UI sees ID and display path; display path is never accepted as write authority. Cancellation mints nothing; rejection leaves existing selection unchanged.

rules.name: Picker race
rules.contract: Capture owner generation before opening native dialog without holding HostState/AppState locks. On return revalidate actual window instance and generation before installing selection. If owner changed, discard selection with STALE_OWNER; do not overwrite new owner state or start persistence.

rules.name: Capability lifetime
rules.contract: Selections are reusable only by their live owner generation and allowed purpose. Reselect invalidates prior unreserved selections. Already reserved request keeps its immutable captured selection for completion; invalidation detaches presentation rather than modifying a submitted request. Cross-window, expired generation and wrong purpose reject before IO.

rules.name: Draft lifetime
rules.contract: Unsaved draft is runtime state only. Cancel/close revokes owner and drops unsaved draft after in-flight captures are detached; no implicit disk save or recursive cleanup. Reopening a saved draft uses explicit native selection plus adopted S2 open, constructs a fresh owner generation and domain projection; no resurrection of prior selection/request authority.

rules.name: Project switch
rules.contract: An actual bound-project change revokes current wizard generation. A picker merely displaying another location is not a project switch. A matching committed wizard result may request binding through the existing authorized project-binding flow; failure leaves persisted evidence and reports committed-but-unbound, never ordinary unchanged failure.

rules.name: Host locks
rules.contract: Preserve existing HostState -> AppState lock order whenever both are needed. Never retain either lock through native dialog or IO. Copy immutable capture under locks, release for IO, reacquire in same order and revalidate generation before installing projection. Exact production seam and concurrency tests remain part of full S3 Skeleton review.

rules.name: Root proof
rules.contract: Native path normalization is infrastructure proof, not WORK normalize_light/case_fold_key identity or a label comparison. Re-check selected root/parent availability and target confinement at save; exclusive create/CAS remains S2+IO authority. No precheck authorizes overwrite or aliases. Exact native canonicalization/reparse policy and failure-injection seam remain an explicit unresolved full-packet gate.

rules.name: Existing authority bridge
rules.contract: Construct adopted DefinitionAuthorityContext only from live trusted selection/session/window record after validation. Nonempty strings and UUID syntax are not authorization. Do not modify S2 context shape or create a second project identity registry. Candidate new wizard state is application-owned, requires adoption, and cannot be inferred from standing implementation permission.

retain outcome then project authorized result

decisions.proposal: Main/local caller policy reuse and one active owner generation; no new WORK registry
Native capability lifetime, stale picker rejection and detach rules
Unsaved cancellation/reopen/project-switch lifecycle and lock/capture boundaries

architecture.hexagonal: UI -> authenticated native command -> DispatchHost wizard owner -> S1/S2 use cases -> existing IO ports
architecture.dependency: Native picker -> trusted observation -> owner-bound selection -> immutable request -> S2 persistence -> authorized UI projection
architecture.ownership: WORK owns registered projects/leases; HOST application owns runtime wizard and request records; domain owns definition; IO owns private journal.
architecture.mutation: Only validated live owner updates wizard draft. UI is projection, not authority. No project settings mutation on begin/select/cancel.
architecture.transaction: Owner reservation is runtime-only; adopted S2/IO commit unchanged; presentation authorization follows retained persistence evidence.
